    1. start(ServerConfig, HttpApp, Effect)

Interface Backend

public interface Backend
An HTTP engine that serves an HttpApp. forj-http has none built in; they're separate modules (forj-http-helidon first), and an app picks one by constructing it. No ServiceLoader: nothing is discovered at runtime.

The contract for an implementation:

  • each request runs on its own virtual thread, which builds a Request (with Method.of(String) and Uri.of(String, String), so common values aren't allocated), calls app.run(request), and runs the result with effect.unsafeRunSync, blocking, on that same thread: no hand-off to another pool;
  • the request body is a stream, limited to ServerConfig.maxBodyBytes(); a larger body is answered with 413 before or while it's read;
  • the response body is written with Body.writeTo(OutputStream), using Body.length() for Content-Length when it's known; then the backend closes its stream, with no flush before that, so an engine that buffers can still send a small body of unknown length in one write with a Content-Length (writeTo already keeps a writer's own flushes from reaching it);
  • if running the app throws (no errors() middleware, or a failure inside it), the client gets a bare 500 and the error is logged; a connection never just closes.
